themes.label: AI Infrastructure / Semis — Sentiment-Driven Dislocation
themes.narrative: The market has been pricing AI-infrastructure semis as one crowded, over-levered trade unwinding on doubt about AI capex durability — KLAC -40.5% from its 52wH, NXT -44.9%, APP -46.9%, all flagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN by the scanner.
themes.dataAnchor: AVGO sits -21.4% from its high at $389.28 with insiders buying $0.37M at the trough and revenue growing 38.7% YoY. NXT is -44.9% off high with revenue +31.6% YoY (recovery confirmed). BWXT is -30.2% off high with revenue +26.1% YoY (recovery confirmed). None of the conviction-tier names show a fundamental deterioration matching the price move.
themes.counterRead: The actual trigger wasn't a US AI-demand story: SK Hynix and Samsung posted Q2 margin compression from Chinese-subsidized competition, which cascaded through Korea's highly leveraged retail options/ETF market into automated margin calls (~$2T in regional market cap erased) and forced a rare joint Japan-Korea currency intervention (USD/JPY near ¥164, won to the 1,410s). That's a competitive-margin and leverage-liquidation shock centered in Korea, not evidence that AI infrastructure demand itself is rolling over — which is why revenue at the US supply-chain names (AVGO, NXT, BWXT) kept confirming growth through the selloff. Treat this as a real but external shock that got mispriced onto US suppliers by association.
themes.watchFor: USD/JPY retesting ¥164 or the won retesting 1,410s would signal the Aug 1 intervention is failing and the leverage-unwind risk is still live, not resolved.

themes.label: Index-Level Calm Masks Real Dispersion — Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: SPY sitting right at its 52-week high reads as 'risk is off the table' at the index level, reinforced by VIX sitting near cycle lows around 16.
themes.dataAnchor: Verified directly: the Magnificent 7 average -14.74% from their own 52-week highs, a 14.74-point gap versus SPY (at its high). It's not uniform — AMZN is now the strongest (-1.3% from high), TSLA the weakest (-34.9%). Bank lending standards (SLOOS) are LOOSE at 0%, well below the ~40% level that historically precedes a confirmed rollover.
themes.counterRead: The index-level calm is ahead of the real dispersion sitting underneath it. Because SPY is cap-weighted, this concentration means a passive SPY position (the largest single holding in this book) is a much more concentrated bet on a handful of names than the 'at its high' headline suggests. Credit being loose means this reads as leadership rotation, not a confirmed top — but the divergence itself is real and the read flips fast if credit tightens.
themes.watchFor: SLOOS net tightening crossing back above ~40% while the Mag7/SPY gap persists — that combination is the historical pre-drawdown pattern, and it hasn't fired yet.

themes.label: Enterprise SaaS — Revenue Confirmed, Verdict Now Sits With Guidance
themes.narrative: A year of 'AI will commoditize SaaS' fear has priced enterprise software as if durable growth is over — HUBS is -54.8% from its 52wH, NOW -42.9%, both flagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN.
themes.dataAnchor: NOW revenue is confirmed growing 23.1% YoY (recovery confirmed). HUBS revenue is up 23%+ YoY and the stock has already staged a real recovery — RSI back to 58.9 and +26.4% over the last month, well ahead of SPY over the same window.
themes.counterRead: The revenue math doesn't support 'growth is over' for either name, but this is now a name-by-name earnings-verdict story, not a sector call — HUBS beat EPS by 29% in May and still gapped down -19% the next session on guidance, proving a beat alone doesn't resolve this. HUBS reports Aug 5, with TWLO/FIVN/NET/TEAM/DBX/DDOG clustered the next day — treat this week as a binary test of the AI-monetization narrative per name, not a read you can extend across the group.
themes.watchFor: HUBS Aug 5 and the Aug 6 SaaS cluster guidance language on AI-driven seat/usage growth — a repeat of the May beat-then-gap-down pattern on any of these names would confirm the market is pricing guidance risk correctly, not being irrational.

themes.label: Restrictive Rates Persisting Despite the Equity Melt-Up
themes.narrative: VIX sitting near cycle lows (~16) and SPY grinding to fresh highs reads as 'the storm has passed' and financial conditions easing.
themes.dataAnchor: 10Y real yield is still ~2.4% (restrictive), 10Y nominal ~4.7%, Fed funds 3.63%, 2s10s curve only around +0.45 — none of these eased alongside the equity rally. HY OAS at 2.84% shows credit isn't stressed, but the discount-rate backdrop itself hasn't loosened.
themes.counterRead: Equities are melting up into a tighter, not looser, rate backdrop — that combination doesn't usually persist cleanly. The 'all-clear' narrative implied by the low VIX is ahead of what the rates data actually shows.
themes.watchFor: Real 10Y yield breaking meaningfully below 2.4%, or the equity rally stalling if it doesn't.

themes.label: Nuclear / Power Infrastructure — Capital Separating Revenue From Story
themes.narrative: Active SMR permitting news (X-Energy vs. BWXT, NuScale vs. GE Vernova coverage) is treating nuclear/power infrastructure as a single overheated theme.
themes.dataAnchor: BWXT is -30.2% off high with revenue +26.1% YoY (recovery confirmed) and NXT -44.9% off high with revenue +31.6% YoY (recovery confirmed) — both durable-moat, revenue-backed suppliers. Meanwhile the speculative, pre-revenue corner of the same theme is getting hit far harder over the last month: CCJ -11.8%, GEV -13.2%, SMR -17.6%, OKLO -26.0%.
themes.counterRead: Capital is already separating revenue-confirmed suppliers from story stocks within this theme — that's the setup continuing from three weeks ago, not a reason for fresh caution on BWXT/NXT specifically.
themes.watchFor: BWXT and NXT's next earnings confirming the revenue-recovery trend continues without margin slippage.

strategyPosture: Hold current exposure. The AI-infrastructure dislocation (AVGO, BWXT, NXT) is genuinely data-confirmed and insider-backed, not just cheap — but treat any new capital as staged, not lump sum, given the Japan/Korea currency intervention is a live, unresolved overhang and this week's SaaS earnings wall (HUBS Aug 5, six more names Aug 6) is a binary per-name test, not a trend you can buy in bulk.
whereWaveBuilds: The next real regime shift shows up first in one of two places: a SLOOS print crossing back above ~40% net tightening (flips Mag7 rotation into a confirmed rollover), or USD/JPY retesting ¥164 (signals the Aug 1 intervention is failing to hold, since it treats Japan's debt-driven yen weakness as a symptom, not the underlying disease).
